title: Customer Clarity Scorer + SLA-Mapped Intake Playbook for Hosted API Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently submit feature requests to Hosted API that combine multiple high-risk signals (streaming + tool calls + structured outputs) but arrive without enough operational or security context. PMs spend disproportionate time clarifying scope, SLA expectations, and compliance needs before routing requests to eng or sales.

Goal: Design a repeatable intake playbook and lightweight automation ("clarity scorer") to rapidly classify inbound enterprise Hosted API feature requests by: customer readiness, required SLA tier, security/compliance gate, and engineering effort band. The output should be a deterministic routing decision that maps requests to: self-serve onboarding, sales-assisted Dedicated/Private, or full-eng roadmap evaluation.

Success criteria: average initial triage time < 24 hours; >50% of enterprise requests routed without manual PM clarification after pilot; reduced PM clarification cycles per ticket from mean 3->1.5; measurable reduction in missed SLA expectations at pilot customers.

Scope: inbound non-bug feature requests for Hosted API that mention chat, streaming, tool/function-calling, or structured outputs. Includes enterprise signups (SAML/SSO, contractual customers) and high-usage tenants.

Out of scope: ad-hoc internal feature requests, bug reports, infra-only requests (capacity/quotas), and partner integration projects handled by Solutions Engineering.

Proposed solution summary:
1) Add a short, conditional questionnaire to the intake form for enterprise requests that dynamically surfaces clarifying fields based on keywords (streaming, tools, structured outputs).
2) Build a lightweight ML-based "clarity scorer" (logistic classifier) that ingests request text + questionnaire and outputs: readiness_score (0-100), sla_recommendation (standard | enterprise-sla | dedicated-lane), security_flag (none | review-needed | embargoed), and effort_bucket (small | medium | large).
3) Map clarity scorer outputs to routing lanes and an auto-generated triage comment that includes: suggested SLA, sample acceptance criteria, required docs (data flow diagram, prompt privacy statement), and next steps for the customer/PM.
4) Create an SLA mapping rubric that ties quantized latency/cost tolerance inputs to specific product offers (hosted default, dedicated, private).
5) Instrument triage telemetry (time-to-route, percent auto-routed, downstream engineering conversions) and add dashboard widgets in Console for PM/Eng leads.

Data & privacy notes: classifier will be trained on anonymized historical intake text and labeled triage outcomes; any raw customer content will be redacted for PII before storage. Work with Security & Compliance to ensure training telemetry is permitted.

Rollout plan: 2-week pilot with 5 pre-selected enterprise accounts; iterative improvements to classifier model and questionnaire UX during pilot; broader rollout conditional on meeting success criteria above.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form surfaces conditional clarifying questions for streaming/tool/structured requests
Clarity scorer returns deterministic outputs for >90% of pilot tickets
Routing rules auto-assign >=50% of pilot enterprise requests without PM edits
Auto-generated triage comment includes required security checklist links and SLA recommendation
Telemetry dashboard shows time-to-route and auto-route rate; data populated for pilot bookings
Security sign-off obtained for training dataset and redaction approach
